title: A.K. Roy v. Union of India (NSA Case)

content.caseIdentity: A.K. Roy v. Union of India, (1982) 1 SCC 271; AIR 1982 SC 710
content.facts: A Constitution Bench considered challenges to the National Security Ordinance, 1980 and National Security Act, 1980, including preventive-detention safeguards and Advisory Board procedure.
questionsBeforeCourt: Whether the ordinance-making power and challenged preventive-detention provisions were constitutionally valid.
What procedural rights a detenu has before an Advisory Board.
content.ratioDecidendi: The Court treated ordinance-making under Article 123 as legislative power subject to constitutional limitations and held that Article 22(3)(b) restricts ordinary legal representation before an Advisory Board, while parity concerns arise if the detaining authority uses legal assistance; assistance by a non-lawyer friend remains possible.
content.holding: The challenged framework was substantially upheld with procedural clarification concerning Advisory Board representation.
content.relevance: Leading Constitution Bench authority on preventive detention, Article 22 and Advisory Board procedure.
